title: Count Primes (Sieve of Eratosthenes)
description:
Return the count of prime numbers less than or equal to `n`. Use the Sieve of Eratosthenes algorithm for efficiency: create a boolean list, start from 2, mark all multiples of each prime as composite.

**Example:**
```
count_primes(10) → 4   # primes: 2, 3, 5, 7
count_primes(1) → 0
count_primes(2) → 1
count_primes(50) → 15
```
hint: Create a list `is_prime` of True values size n+1. Set 0 and 1 to False. For i from 2 to sqrt(n), if is_prime[i], mark all multiples starting at i*i as False. Count the True values.
